# 1 Kings Chapter 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-ʾet-his-own-house Solomon built thirteen years, and-he-finished ʾet-all his-house.

**2** And-he-built ʾet-the-House-of the-Forest-of Lebanon — a-hundred cubits its-length, and-fifty cubits its-width, and-thirty cubits its-height, upon four rows-of cedar pillars, and-cedar beams upon the-pillars.

**3** And-it-was-roofed with-cedar above upon the-chambers that were upon the-pillars — forty-five; fifteen in-a-row.

**4** And-window-frames were in-three rows, and-window-opening opposite window-opening, three times.

**5** And-all the-openings and-the-doorposts were squared with-frames, and-window-opening opposite window-opening, three times.

**6** And-the-Hall-of-Pillars he-made — fifty cubits its-length, and-thirty cubits its-width. And-a-porch was before-them, and-pillars and-a-threshold before-them.

**7** And-the-Hall-of-the-Throne where he-judged — the-Hall-of-Judgment — he-made. And-it-was-covered with-cedar from-the-floor to-the-floor.

**8** And-his-house where he-dwelt — the-other court within the-hall — was-of-the-same workmanship. And-a-house he-made for-the-daughter-of Pharaoh — whom Solomon had-taken — like this hall.

**9** All these were-of costly stones, according-to-the-measures-of hewn-stone, sawed with-the-saw, inside and-outside, and-from the-foundation to the-coping, and-from-outside to the-great court.

**10** And-the-foundation was-of costly stones, great stones — stones-of ten cubits and-stones-of eight cubits.

**11** And-above were costly stones, according-to-the-measures-of hewn-stone, and-cedar.

**12** And-the-great court all-around — three rows-of hewn-stone and-a-row-of cedar beams. And-so for-the-inner court-of the-house-of YHWH and-for-the-porch-of the-house.

**13** And-the-king Solomon sent and-took Hiram from-Tyre.

**14** He was the-son-of a-widow woman from-the-tribe-of Naphtali, and-his-father was a-man-of Tyre, a-worker-of bronze. And-he-was-filled with the-wisdom and-the-understanding and-the-knowledge to-do all work in-bronze. And-he-came to the-king Solomon and-did ʾet-all his-work.

**15** And-he-fashioned ʾet-the-two pillars-of bronze — eighteen cubits the-height-of the-one pillar, and-a-cord-of twelve cubits encircled ʾet-the-second pillar.

**16** And-two capitals he-made to-set upon the-tops-of the-pillars, cast-of bronze — five cubits the-height-of the-one capital, and-five cubits the-height-of the-second capital.

**17** Nets-of network, twisted-work-of chains, for-the-capitals that were upon the-top-of the-pillars — seven for-the-one capital and-seven for-the-second capital.

**18** And-he-made ʾet-the-pillars, and-two rows all-around upon the-one network to-cover ʾet-the-capitals that were upon the-top with-the-pomegranates. And-so he-did for-the-second capital.

**19** And-the-capitals that were upon the-top-of the-pillars were-of lily work in-the-hall — four cubits.

**20** And-capitals on the-two pillars, also above, close-by the-belly that was beside the-network. And-the-pomegranates were two-hundred, in-rows all-around, upon the-second capital.

**21** And-he-set-up ʾet-the-pillars at-the-porch-of the-temple. And-he-set-up ʾet-the-right pillar and-called its-name Jachin. And-he-set-up ʾet-the-left pillar and-called its-name Boaz.

**22** And-upon the-top-of the-pillars was lily work. And-the-work-of the-pillars was-finished.

**23** And-he-made ʾet-the-Sea, cast — ten cubits from-its-brim to-its-brim, round all-around, and-five cubits its-height, and-a-line-of thirty cubits encircled ʾet-it all-around.

**24** And-gourds beneath its-brim all-around encircled-it — ten in-a-cubit, encircling ʾet-the-Sea all-around. The-gourds were in-two rows, cast in-its-casting.

**25** It-stood upon twelve oxen — three facing north, and-three facing west, and-three facing south, and-three facing east. And-the-Sea was upon-them above, and-all their-hindquarters were inward.

**26** And-its-thickness was a-handbreadth, and-its-brim was-like the-work-of the-brim-of a-cup, a-flower-of a-lily. Two-thousand baths it-held.

**27** And-he-made ʾet-the-ten stands-of bronze — four cubits the-length-of the-one stand, and-four cubits its-width, and-three cubits its-height.

**28** And-this was the-work-of the-stand: they-had panels, and-the-panels were between the-frames.

**29** And-on the-panels that were between the-frames were lions, oxen, and-cherubim. And-on the-frames — above and-below the-lions and-the-oxen — were wreaths-of hanging-work.

**30** And-four wheels-of bronze belonged-to the-one stand, and-axles-of bronze. And-its-four feet had supports — beneath the-basin the-supports were cast, with-wreaths at-the-side-of each.

**31** And-its-mouth from-within the-crown and-above was a-cubit. And-its-mouth was round like-the-work-of a-stand — a-cubit and-a-half. And-also upon its-mouth were carvings, and-their-panels were square, not round.

**32** And-the-four wheels were beneath the-panels, and-the-axles-of the-wheels were in-the-stand. And-the-height-of the-one wheel was a-cubit and-a-half.

**33** And-the-work-of the-wheels was like-the-work-of a-chariot wheel — their-axles and-their-rims and-their-spokes and-their-hubs — all were cast.

**34** And-four supports were at-the-four corners-of the-one stand; from the-stand were its-supports.

**35** And-on-the-top-of the-stand — half a-cubit in-height, round all-around — and-on the-top-of the-stand, its-stays and-its-panels were from-it.

**36** And-he-engraved on the-plates-of its-stays and-on its-panels cherubim, lions, and-palm-trees, according-to-the-space-of each, with-wreaths all-around.

**37** Like-this he-made ʾet-the-ten stands — one casting, one measure, one form for-all-of-them.

**38** And-he-made ten basins-of bronze — forty baths each basin held. Four cubits was each basin. One basin was on each stand, for-the-ten stands.

**39** And-he-set ʾet-the-stands — five on the-south side-of the-house and-five on the-north side-of the-house. And-ʾet-the-Sea he-set on the-south side-of the-house, eastward, toward the-south.

**40** And-Hiram made ʾet-the-basins and-ʾet-the-shovels and-ʾet-the-bowls. And-Hiram finished doing all the-work that he-did for-the-king Solomon for-the-house-of YHWH:

**41** the-two pillars and-the-bowls-of the-capitals that were on-the-top-of the-two pillars, and-the-two networks to-cover ʾet-the-two bowls-of the-capitals that were on-the-top-of the-pillars,

**42** and-the-four-hundred pomegranates for-the-two networks — two rows-of pomegranates for-the-one network — to-cover ʾet-the-two bowls-of the-capitals that were upon the-face-of the-pillars,

**43** and-the-ten stands and-the-ten basins upon the-stands,

**44** and-the-one Sea and-the-twelve oxen beneath the-Sea,

**45** and-the-pots and-the-shovels and-the-bowls. And-all these vessels that Hiram made for-the-king Solomon for-the-house-of YHWH were-of burnished bronze.

**46** In-the-plain-of the-Jordan the-king cast-them, in-the-clay-ground between Succoth and-Zarethan.

**47** And-Solomon left all the-vessels unweighed, because-of the-very great multitude — the-weight-of the-bronze was-not searched-out.

**48** And-Solomon made all the-vessels that were in-the-house-of YHWH: the-altar-of gold, and-the-table upon which was the-bread-of the-Presence — of-gold,

**49** and-the-lampstands — five on-the-right and-five on-the-left before the-inner-sanctuary — of-refined gold, and-the-flowers and-the-lamps and-the-tongs — of-gold,

**50** and-the-cups and-the-snuffers and-the-bowls and-the-spoons and-the-firepans — of-refined gold, and-the-hinges for-the-doors-of the-inner house, the-Holy-of-Holies, and-for-the-doors-of the-house, the-temple — of-gold.

**51** And-all the-work that the-king Solomon did for-the-house-of YHWH was-finished. And-Solomon brought-in ʾet-the-holy-things-of David his-father — the-silver and-the-gold and-the-vessels — he-put in-the-treasuries-of the-house-of YHWH.

---
## EMET Textual Notes

1. **7:1 — "thirteen years"**: Solomon spent thirteen years on his palace versus seven on the temple. The narrator makes no comment, but the comparison invites one.

2. **7:14 — Hiram the craftsman**: Not to be confused with King Hiram. This Hiram is half-Israelite (Naphtali) and half-Phoenician (Tyre) — "filled with wisdom and understanding and knowledge," echoing the language used for Bezalel in Exodus 31:3.

3. **7:21 — "Jachin... Boaz"**: The pillar names likely mean "He establishes" and "In Him is strength." They are theological statements cast in bronze at the temple entrance.

4. **7:23-26 — the-Sea**: A massive bronze basin (~10,000 gallons) resting on twelve oxen facing the four compass points. This is a cosmological symbol — the primordial waters tamed and ordered for liturgical use.

5. **7:47 — "the-weight was-not searched-out"**: The quantity of bronze was so vast it could not be weighed. This extravagance reflects both Solomon's wealth and the theology that no expense is excessive for God's dwelling.

— EMET
